newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity rises on Western unit outages.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity rises on Western unit outages.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were pulled higher Wednesday by strong front-month trade due to several generation unit outages in the U.S. West, industry sources said.
"(The price rise) can best be attributed to short-term operational issues," said one Houston-based futures trader, adding "There is a lot of capacity out (in the West) right now."
As of 1220 EST, April California-Oregon Border (COB) was trading up 69 cents at the day's high of $11.60 per megawatt hour (MWh), from trade as low as $11.10 per MWh.
May COB was trading up 35 cents at $10.95 from exchanges in a range of $10.80-11.00 per MWh.
June COB was trading steady, while August and September were both up 10 cents at $18.15 and $18.25, respectively.
April Palo Verde (PV) was trading up 56 cents at $15.80 following exchanges as low as $15.60, while May PV was up 33 cents at $15.15 from trade as high as $15.20 per MWh.
August and September PV were up nine and five cents, to $24.15 and $22.10, respectively.
A 550 megawatt (MW) unit at the Jim Bridger coal-fired generating complex in Wyoming was heard shut late yesterday, and expected to restart Thursday.
A 750 megawatt (MW) unit at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico was also scheduled to resume operation Thursday after being shut Tuesday for repairs.
A 350 MW San Juan coal-fired unit also in New Mexico was shut Sunday, with an unknown restart date.
In addition to coal unit outages, the 1,070 MW San Onofre nuclear unit 2 in San Clemente, Calif., was shut and set to startup March 20.
Arizona Public's 1,221 MW Palo Verde nuclear unit 3 was expected to return to service from a scheduled maintenance and refueling shutdown in early April.

Also, some hydroelectric projects in the Northwest have scaled back production in preparation for fish migration next month or in line with lower snowpack figures in some mountainous parts of the West.
Bonneville Power Administration said Wednesday it was raising firm, peak power prices for Thursday delivery by $1.50 per MWh to $16.50 at the California Oregon Border.
As of 1230 EST, NYMEX April Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading up 3.7 cents at $1.956 per million British thermal units.
Cool, wet conditions are expected in the Northwest through Friday with temperatures averaging four to eight degrees Fahrenheit below normal.
Most of the Southwest would enjoy dry and much above normal temperatures through to the weekend.
COB open interest for March 11 rose 19 to 3,525, while PV open interest rose 117 to 2,918, NYMEX said.
